B6.1.1.3 (Sub-Strand 1) covers factors, multiples and prime numbers 1-100, with bounded source context showing indicators on determining HCF and LCM of two or three numbers using prime factorisation. B6.1.3.1 (Sub-Strand 3) covers strategies for comparing, adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing common, decimal and percent fractions, which operationally depend on locating common denominators (LCM) and simplifying to lowest terms (HCF). Proficiency with factors/multiples/prime factorisation therefore supports success with the fraction-operation strategies, giving a same-rank first_to_second developmental direction. judgment.rationale: Both are Indicators in Strand 'Geometry and Measurement' / Sub-Strand 'Geometric Reasoning', so the grain matches. B5.3.4.2.2 (BASIC 5, rank 1) asks learners to identify images of a single transformation limited to reflection of a 2D shape in a plane; B6.3.3.5.2 (BASIC 6, rank 2) asks the same identification task but broadened to reflection AND translation, under the BASIC 6 content standard 'Perform a single transformation (i.e. reflection translation) on a 2D shape'. This is substantive extension of the same skill to an additional transformation type at the higher configured grade, so proficiency with the BASIC 5 reflection indicator supports success on the BASIC 6 indicator; direction is lower-to-higher rank (second_to_first). The shared Learning Component 'Identify images of a reflection of a 2D shape in a plane' confirms the overlapping skill core rather than mere wording similarity. Note the BASIC 6 parent content standard carries a same-code/different-content audit flag for B6.3.3.5, but the transformation-focused text used here is unambiguous.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (rank 1, same grade coordinate) under Strand 3: Geometry and Measurement, but in different sub-strands: B5.3.4.2.2 (Geometric Reasoning) asks learners to identify images of a single transformation (reflection) of 2D shapes in a plane, while B5.3.1.1.1 (Lines and Shapes) asks learners to demonstrate understanding of properties (sides, angles, diagonals) of squares and rectangles. The LCs confirm distinct skill content (reflection/image identification vs. quadrilateral property analysis); shared tokens are generic ('of', 'e') and the shared code segments ('b5','3') only reflect grade and strand. There is substantive conceptual coherence — both concern attributes of 2D plane figures, and property knowledge supports recognising congruent reflected images — but the evidence does not establish that proficiency in either specifically supports success in the other, and same-rank placement provides no directional warrant. relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment rather than a directional buildsTowards.
